coordination_failures: Severe underutilization of resources (0% utilization) despite high demand and frequent requests.
Critical shortage of repair crews led to pool exhaustion (63 times), directly contributing to mission failure.
Repeated rejections of road repair requests (10 times) hindered access and response efficiency.
Harbor sector suffered cascading failures due to unaddressed infrastructure needs across three missions.
headline: Harbor Infrastructure Failures Led to High Casualties Despite Overall Mission Completion

key_moments.description: Four high-severity missions launched simultaneously, overwhelming initial capacity.
Mission m4 (harbor infra, sev=3) failed—first and only mission failure—triggering increased losses in later harbor missions.
Wave of new missions (m10–m12) began, straining already depleted repair resources.
Final mission (m9) resolved with poor outcome: 1 saved vs. 9 lost, highlighting persistent harbor access issues.

lessons: Pre-position repair crews in critical zones like harbors before disaster onset.
Prioritize road repair approvals to maintain access for emergency services.
Balance mission load early to avoid cascading infrastructure failures.
Track and forecast resource exhaustion to prevent operational collapse.
Improve coordination between medical and infrastructure teams to reduce preventable losses.
what_worked: Early medical surge responses were effective, resolving missions within 4-5 ticks with minimal loss.
Industrial and residential infrastructure repairs (excluding harbor) generally succeeded with good save ratios.
All but one mission were resolved; panic remained relatively low at 0.18.
